_enums._comment: The closed vocabularies. Free-text fields are written as null in this template on purpose -- a specimen string is a string somebody ships verbatim -- which left these values learnable only by being rejected. They are listed here and checked by scripts/check_plan_contract.py, which reads them from render_final_trip_html.py rather than from this block, so the two cannot drift: tests/test_plan_contract.py fails if this list stops matching.

_contract: Notes on the three blocks a real run shipped without. All three are OPTIONAL -- a plan that
omits them passes every gate exactly as before -- so nothing warns you when they are absent.
That is the whole reason they are written out here.
trip.traveler_constraints -- what the traveller's body and diet require, carried from intake.
dietary_or_religious_needs and mobility_notes are free text lists. allergy_severity is one of
none | preference | intolerance | severe, and it is the difference between a dish the traveller
would rather skip and one that ends the trip. allergy_card_text is the literal sentence handed
to restaurant staff, in the local language. max_continuous_walking_minutes is a hard number the
walking check reads: with it set, any single segment or activity that exceeds it fails the gate,
and without it nothing measures the constraint the traveller actually stated.
entry_context -- the entry conclusion, on the page. SKILL.md's own quality gate requires that
the conclusion reach the page through this block, and this template, the skeleton and the HTML
template all omitted it, so a real cross-border plan shipped with no entry section at all during
reintroduced Schengen border checks. status is one of not_required | required_held |
required_to_apply | unverified. traveler_basis is a status CATEGORY -- 'EU long-term residence
permit holder' -- and never a document number or expiry date: it goes onto a page the traveller
may share, and a category is what makes the conclusion rereadable a month later anyway.
Delete the whole block when the trip never crosses a border; an unverified entry panel on a
domestic trip is noise, and SKILL.md says not to raise entry as a blocker for a traveller
staying home.
days[].activities[].on_foot_minutes -- minutes of THIS activity spent on foot or standing,
an integer >= 0. Segment walking_minutes covers only travel between stops, so a page can
truthfully print '42 minutes on foot' for a day that schedules three and a half hours of it
inside museums and markets. That happened, against a stated mobility limit, and the walking
gate certified the number. Authoring it turns the second half of the day's walking on.
intake_context -- REQUIRED, unlike the three blocks above. method is one of html_form |
user_supplied | chat_fallback and each carries its own evidence: html_form names the intake
file only the intake server writes; user_supplied says what the traveller supplied instead;
chat_fallback carries declined_verbatim, the traveller's OWN WORDS declining the form, plus
declined_at. It is required because the failure it guards is an omission: an assistant that
skipped the form is the same assistant that would leave an optional key out, so an optional
version would report clean on exactly the run that motivated it.
attraction_tickets[].sale_opens_at -- REQUIRED on any ticket an activity actually schedules,
and only those: a ticket listed as an option nobody put on a day cannot strand anyone. status is
always_available | scheduled_release | at_the_door | sold_out_or_unavailable. opens_at is an ISO
date-time and is required when status is scheduled_release. basis is one sentence saying where
the rule came from -- it is the whole anti-rubber-stamp of this field, because someone who
opened the official page can write it and someone who guessed 'always_available' cannot. A
guessed value is a fabricated fact, which is worse than the blank this field replaces.

sources[].confidence -- OPTIONAL, and a CLOSED ENUM when present: high | medium | low |
    researched | unverified. It is printed as visible text beside the source, so it has to be
    translatable; it was free text until a Chinese page shipped 「… · high」 in an otherwise
    fully Chinese register with every gate green. Omitting it renders "researched" in the trip's
    language. Any qualification -- "fare requires recheck", "timetable is seasonal" -- belongs in
    claim_or_decision_supported beside it, which is the field for saying what a source proves.
trip.traveler_constraints.untyped_constraints -- the marker that says which of these fields
NOBODY HAS TYPED YET, as opposed to answered. It is empty here on purpose, and that empty
object is what makes the allergy_severity "none" above honest: 'none' is a claim that there is
nothing to avoid, and the empty marker is how this file says a person made that claim. It is
written by new_plan_skeleton.py as one entry per untyped field, because the intake collects
both fields as prose and nothing turns a sentence into an enum or a number. Delete an entry
when you type its field, or delete the whole key; {}, [], "", false and 0 all read as
'nothing is untyped'. While an entry remains, check_untyped_constraints refuses the plan by
name, check_walking_budget stops calling a null cap the traveller's answer, and the light
verification tier is withheld -- an untyped constraint is an open question and never a clean
bill of health. This key was live in all four of those places while this contract said nothing
about it, so an author copying this file met a refusal for a key they had never seen.
trip.intake_changes -- OPTIONAL, empty unless the traveller changed something after the form.
One {field, intake_value, plan_value, reason} per change; field is dietary_or_religious_needs |
mobility_notes | traveler_count | cap_per_person, the four limits check_plan_consistency compares
with the intake file. A plan that differs from its intake on one of them without an entry here
is refused, because a dropped allergy and a legitimately raised cap look identical from the
plan alone. The reason is printed beside the traveller's constraints: it is their change.
booking_options.ground_transport[].origin_station_id / destination_station_id -- OPTIONAL. The
provider's own identifier for a station, for a search that keys stations by id rather than by
name (Trainline writes urn:trainline:generic:loc:6386). A declared-prefilled origin or
destination is carried when the URL holds the station's name as a whole value OR this id; with
neither, the button promises a filled search it does not open.
imagery_sidecar -- OPTIONAL and NOT written by hand: `python scripts/fetch_plan_imagery.py
<plan.json>` sets it to the sidecar's file name, relative to the plan, and moves the photo
bytes out of the plan (they cost ~576k tokens to carry inline). null or absent, as shipped
here, means every reader looks for <plan-stem>-imagery.json beside the plan and renders
without photographs if there is none. A name that points at no file is refused loudly rather
than rendered around, because no gate counts images and a silently photo-less page is one
nobody notices.

booking_options.flights[].outbound_itinerary.self_transfer / return_itinerary.self_transfer -- true only on a leg whose connection is on separate tickets (written by kiwi_flights.py when the traveller accepted self-transfer); the page prints a warning on that card.
booking_options.flights[].price_note -- how to read the per-person price when it is an average over a party with children or infants; printed beside the price.
trip.traveler_preferences.accepts_self_transfer -- the traveller's OWN WORDS accepting separate-ticket connections; required before any leg is marked self_transfer.

booking_options.flights[].origin_place_id / destination_place_id -- the search provider's own key for each place when its URL names places that way (Kiwi.com: amsterdam-netherlands); the prefilled-field check accepts the id in place of the airport code, as it accepts a rail card's station ids.

bookings -- one record per group the traveller decided: {option_id, state: chosen|booked, booked_on (YYYY-MM-DD, booked only), booked_via (booked only), paid_total and paid_currency (optional, booked only)}. Never a booking reference, document or payment detail. Groups: flights/ground by leg_group_id, hotels by stay_group_id, rental cars one group, each ticket alone. Written by scripts/record_booking.py; outside verification.

trip.timezone / trip.origin_timezone -- IANA time zones (Europe/London) of the destination and of where the traveller leaves from; days[].timezone overrides trip.timezone for a day on a multi-zone trip. The calendar writes UTC from them; without them it is floating, which only Apple Calendar shows as written.

booking_options.flights[] / ground_transport[] .outbound_itinerary / .return_itinerary .departure_timezone / .arrival_timezone -- required on every itinerary when the plan names more than one zone, optional on a single-zone trip; departure + duration_minutes must land on the arrival in the arrival zone (30-minute tolerance).

days[].dining[].reservation_need -- required | recommended | walk_in | not_accepted; the calendar reminds the day before for required and recommended. The queue note stays the sentence the traveller reads.
Delete this _contract key before saving the real plan.

traveler_preferences._comment: What the traveller asked FOR, as opposed to traveler_constraints, which is what they cannot have. Both come off the same intake form and only one of them used to survive into the plan: the skill remembered the allergy and forgot the reason for the trip. ranked_must_haves is the binding half -- every entry must be answered by an anchor that names it, or by an entry in unmet_preferences saying why the season or the place cannot deliver it.

per_jurisdiction._note: One record per jurisdiction the trip ENTERS, for a trip that enters more than one. The flat fields above stay the single-jurisdiction form and are unchanged. A trip whose stops declare two jurisdictions and carries one entry answer is confidently wrong about the second, and an entry answer is what decides whether the traveller boards.

arrival_essentials._note: What the traveller needs in the first hour on the ground, and the part of a trip this skill used to say nothing about. Every other block here is about the days; none of them answered 'can I pay', 'can I get online', 'who do I call'. Each entry is researched and dated like any other fact -- never written from memory -- or marked not_applicable with a reason. `status` is one of researched / unverified / not_applicable.

payment._note: Will the traveller's cards work, and how much cash do they need? A card that is declined at the first ticket machine is a trip that starts badly, and the answer differs by country far more than travellers expect.

connectivity._note: Can they get online on arrival, and can they charge the phone that holds this page? A dead or offline phone is a navigation failure, not an inconvenience.

emergency._note: The local emergency number, and -- when the traveller is abroad -- the consulate or embassy of their own nationality with a contact that works. Both are facts about a specific country and a specific passport, so both are researched, never recalled.

health_and_insurance._note: Whether the traveller carries cover, what the destination expects, and what a visit costs without it. Schengen visa applicants are required to hold travel medical insurance, which makes this an entry question and not only a prudence one.

ground_transport._note: Rail, coach and ferry. Same evidence as a flight, because the traveller asks the same questions -- which service, when, how long, how many changes, what the fare allows -- and on a rail trip this is the largest and most time-sensitive purchase on the page. Omit the array entirely when the trip has no ticketed intercity leg. Every value below is null on purpose: the block once shipped '0' durations, a '0-0' fare and 1970-01-01 stamps as placeholders, and each of those is a value the validator accepts, so an author who missed one shipped a card advertising a 0-minute journey at EUR 0 priced in 1970 with every gate green. Fields to fill: provider (must own review_url); origin_station / destination_station; outbound_date / return_date (ISO, inside the trip window); both itineraries (service identifier, local times, positive duration_minutes, changes, interchange note); material_conditions -- refundable? changeable? is a seat reservation compulsory or extra?; availability_status (available|limited|unknown); fare_low/fare_high/fare_currency; price_status; station_transfer_note -- how they get from the arrival station into town, the ground analogue of an airport transfer, so a cheap fare cannot hide an impractical arrival; and the dated round-trip search URL with its provider and check stamp. travel_class, seat_reservation and single_option_reason are optional display fields -- nothing validates them, but travel_class and seat_reservation are what the card prints beside the dates, and single_option_reason is required in practice whenever this is the only candidate.

venue_hours_by_weekday._comment: Optional and sharper than venue_hours. One key per weekday, mon..sun. A time window like '11:00-22:00' (or two, '11:00-15:00, 17:00-21:00'); the word 'closed' (or 休息) for a day the venue is shut; null or omitted means not filled in, and the flattened venue_hours governs instead. When present, the gate checks the meal against the weekday it is actually scheduled on and the page prints that day's hours -- venue_hours has to be the narrowest window that holds every day, so on its own it shows the traveller less than was researched, and can refuse a meal that is fine.
